chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, and Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When you intend to leave Mecca and go to your family, bid farewell to the House, and perform Tawaf around the House for seven circuits. If you are able to touch the Black Stone and the Yemeni Corner in each circuit, do so; otherwise, begin with it and end with it. If you cannot do that, then it is permissible for you to do what you can.
Then go to the Mustajar (the spot where the door opens into the House) and do there as you did on the day you arrived in Mecca, and choose for yourself from the supplications.

Then touch the Black Stone, then press your belly against the House, placing one hand on the Stone and the other on what is near the door. Praise Allah, extol Him, and send blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).

Then say: 'O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad, Your servant, Your Messenger, Your Prophet, Your Trustworthy, Your Beloved, Your Confidant, and Your Chosen one from Your creation. O Allah, as he delivered Your messages, and strove in Your way, and proclaimed Your command, and was harmed for Your sake, and worshipped You until certainty came to him.'
O Allah, turn me back successful, victorious, answered for me with the best of what any of Your delegates returns with, from forgiveness, blessing, mercy, pleasure, and well-being.
O Allah, if You cause me to die, forgive me; and if You keep me alive, grant me it next year. O Allah, do not make this the last visit to Your House.

O Allah, I am Your servant, son of Your servant, and son of Your maid. You carried me on Your beasts and journeyed me through Your lands until You brought me to Your Sanctuary and Your security. And it was in my good opinion of You that You would forgive my sins.

So if You have already forgiven my sins, increase Your pleasure with me and bring me close to You in position, and do not distance me. And if You have not forgiven me, then from now on, forgive me before my home departs from Your House.
For this is the time of my departure, if You have permitted me, not turning away from You nor from Your House, nor being replaced by You nor by it.

O Allah, protect me from before me, behind me, to my right, and to my left, until You bring me to my family. So when You bring me to my family, suffice me from the burden of Your servants and my dependents, for You are the Guardian of that from Your creation and from me.
Then go to Zamzam and drink from its water. Then exit and say: 'We are the returners, the repentant, the worshippers to our Lord, praising to our Lord, wishing to Allah, returning, if Allah wills.'

He said: 'And indeed, when Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) bid farewell to it and intended to exit from the Sacred Mosque, he fell prostrate at the door of the Mosque for a long time. Then he stood and exited.'

key_terms.الْمُسْتَجَارَ: The Mustajar (the spot where the door opens into the Kaaba)

ai.seo_question: What is the proper way to bid farewell to the Kaaba when leaving Mecca?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the comprehensive etiquette for Tawaf al-Wada' (Farewell Circumambulation), emphasizing the spiritual significance of concluding one's pilgrimage with devotion at the Kaaba. It prescribes specific rituals such as kissing or gesturing to the Black Stone and Yemeni Corner, offering a detailed supplication at the Mustajar (the door of the Kaaba), and drinking from Zamzam before departing. The narration highlights the Imam’s personal example of prostration at the mosque door, reinforcing the practice as a recommended act of gratitude and anticipation for a return.
